name: socket()
description: Creates an endpoint for network communication. The kernel allocates a new socket object, selects the appropriate protocol family implementation (e.g., AF_INET for IPv4), and initializes protocol-specific state including the send/receive buffer queues and protocol operation vectors.
signature: int socket(int domain, int type, int protocol)

main_flow.title: User Space
main_flow.description: The user-space program invokes socket(AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM, 0) via the C library wrapper. The syscall number (NR_socket = 41 on x86-64) is placed in %rax, with domain in %rdi, type in %rsi, and protocol in %rdx, then the syscall instruction traps into the kernel.

detail_nodes.title: glibc socket() wrapper
detail_nodes.description: The GNU C Library provides a thin wrapper around the raw syscall. It sets up the ABI-defined calling convention: %rax = __NR_socket (41), %rdi = domain (AF_INET = 2), %rsi = type (SOCK_STREAM = 1), %rdx = protocol (0 = IPPROTO_IP). No kernel involvement yet.

detail_nodes.title: syscall instruction
detail_nodes.description: The syscall instruction atomically saves %rip and %rflags into MSR_LSTAR-defined kernel entry, switches to ring 0, and loads the kernel stack pointer from the TSS. Control jumps to the system_call entry point in entry_64.S.

source_ref.snippet:
ENTRY(system_call)
  SWAPGS_UNSAFE_STACK
  movq %rsp, PER_CPU_VAR(old_rsp)
  movq PER_CPU_VAR(kernel_stack),%rsp

detail_nodes.title: Socket parameters
detail_nodes.description: The domain parameter selects the address family (AF_INET for IPv4, AF_INET6 for IPv6, AF_UNIX for local). The type parameter selects the socket semantics (SOCK_STREAM for TCP, SOCK_DGRAM for UDP, SOCK_RAW for raw IP). The protocol parameter is usually 0 to let the kernel pick the default protocol for the domain+type combination.

main_flow.title: Kernel Entry
main_flow.description: The generic syscall dispatch routes NR_socket to sys_socket(), which is the kernel entry point. sys_socket() validates the domain, type, and protocol parameters, then calls sock_create() to begin the actual socket object allocation.

detail_nodes.title: SYSCALL_DEFINE3(socket, ...)
detail_nodes.description: sys_socket() is defined with the SYSCALL_DEFINE3 macro in net/socket.c. It calls sock_create() to create the socket object, then calls sock_map_fd() to allocate a file descriptor and associate it with the new socket.

detail_nodes.title: sock_create()
detail_nodes.description: sock_create() is the central socket creation function. It calls __sock_create() which looks up the net_proto_family for the given address family, validates the socket type flags, and then calls the family's create method to allocate protocol-specific state.

detail_nodes.title: sock_map_fd() — socket → fd
detail_nodes.description: sock_map_fd() allocates a new file descriptor via get_unused_fd_flags(), creates a struct file via sock_alloc_file(), and installs the fd→file mapping via fd_install(). The struct file's f_op is set to socket_file_ops, so subsequent read/write/close syscalls on this fd are routed to socket operations.

main_flow.title: AF_INET Protocol Family
main_flow.description: For AF_INET (IPv4), the kernel dispatches to inet_create() in net/ipv4/af_inet.c. This function validates the socket type against the registered protocol table, allocates a struct sock (the generic socket state), and initializes the TCP or UDP protocol-specific state including the operation vectors.

detail_nodes.title: inet_create()
detail_nodes.description: inet_create() is the AF_INET family's create method. It searches the inetsw_array for a matching protocol (TCP for SOCK_STREAM, UDP for SOCK_DGRAM), validates that the protocol supports the requested socket type, and then calls sk_alloc() to allocate the generic sock structure.

detail_nodes.title: sk_alloc() — allocate struct sock
detail_nodes.description: sk_alloc() allocates memory for the protocol-specific sock structure from the socket slab cache. For TCP this is a struct tcp_sock (which embeds struct inet_sock, which embeds struct sock). The allocation uses kmem_cache_alloc() with GFP_KERNEL.

detail_nodes.title: struct proto_ops — inet_stream_ops
detail_nodes.description: The socket layer's struct proto_ops vector defines high-level operations like bind, connect, listen, accept, and sendmsg. For AF_INET SOCK_STREAM, the socket's ops are set to inet_stream_ops, which delegates to the transport protocol (TCP) for the actual work.

source_ref.snippet:
const struct proto_ops inet_stream_ops = {
  .family       = PF_INET,
  .owner        = THIS_MODULE,
  .release      = inet_release,
  .bind         = inet_bind,
  .connect      = inet_stream_connect,
  .socketpair   = sock_no_socketpair,
  .accept       = inet_accept,
  .getname      = inet_getname,
  .poll         = tcp_poll,
  .ioctl        = inet_ioctl,
  .listen       = inet_listen,
  .shutdown     = inet_shutdown,
  .setsockopt   = sock_common_setsockopt,
  .getsockopt   = sock_common_getsockopt,
  .sendmsg      = tcp_sendmsg,
  .recvmsg      = inet_recvmsg,
  .mmap         = sock_no_mmap,
  .sendpage     = tcp_sendpage,
  .splice_read  = tcp_splice_read,
};

detail_nodes.title: struct proto — tcp_prot
detail_nodes.description: The transport protocol's struct proto vector defines low-level operations like connect, disconnect, accept, and the socket state machine callbacks. For TCP, tcp_prot provides the protocol-specific methods that the socket layer calls through.

source_ref.snippet:
struct proto tcp_prot = {
  .name           = "TCP",
  .owner          = THIS_MODULE,
  .close          = tcp_close,
  .connect        = tcp_v4_connect,
  .disconnect     = tcp_disconnect,
  .accept         = inet_csk_accept,
  .ioctl          = tcp_ioctl,
  .init           = tcp_v4_init_sock,
  .destroy        = tcp_v4_destroy_sock,
  .shutdown       = tcp_shutdown,
  .setsockopt     = tcp_setsockopt,
  .getsockopt     = tcp_getsockopt,
  .recvmsg        = tcp_recvmsg,
  .sendmsg        = tcp_sendmsg,
  .backlog_rcv    = tcp_v4_do_rcv,
  ...
};

main_flow.title: Bind / Connect Setup
main_flow.description: After socket creation, the application typically calls bind() to associate the socket with a local address and port, then connect() to establish a connection to a remote peer. bind() sets the local address in inet_sock; connect() initiates the TCP three-way handshake via tcp_v4_connect().

detail_nodes.title: inet_bind()
detail_nodes.description: inet_bind() validates the local address and port, checks for port conflicts using the port hash table (tcp_hashinfo.bhash), and stores the local address in inet->inet_saddr and the port in inet->inet_sport. If port is 0, the kernel auto-allocates an ephemeral port.

detail_nodes.title: tcp_v4_connect()
detail_nodes.description: tcp_v4_connect() is the TCP connect handler for IPv4. It validates the destination address, initializes the TCP state machine (moves to TCP_SYN_SENT), builds and sends the SYN packet via tcp_connect(), and starts the retransmission timer. The actual packet transmission goes through the IP layer.

detail_nodes.title: Socket state machine
detail_nodes.description: A TCP socket progresses through states: CLOSED → SYN_SENT → ESTABLISHED (after receiving SYN-ACK). Each state transition is protected by the socket lock (sk->sk_lock.slock) and triggers callbacks in the protocol state machine. The socket() call itself only creates the socket in the CLOSED state.

main_flow.title: sk_buff Allocation
main_flow.description: Network data in Linux is carried in sk_buff (socket buffer) structures. When the socket is created, the send and receive buffer size limits (sk_sndbuf, sk_rcvbuf) are initialized from system defaults. When data is ready to send, alloc_skb() allocates an sk_buff from the slab cache, which holds packet data, protocol headers, and control metadata.

detail_nodes.title: alloc_skb() — allocate socket buffer
detail_nodes.description: alloc_skb() allocates a new sk_buff structure and its associated data buffer from the slab cache. The sk_buff is the universal packet container in Linux networking, holding packet data, protocol headers at various layers, and control metadata like timestamps and routing info.

detail_nodes.title: struct sk_buff layout
detail_nodes.description: struct sk_buff is a doubly-linked list node with head/tail pointers for data, transport header, network header, and MAC header. It also carries socket ownership (sk), device info (dev), routing info (dst_entry), and checksum state. The data area is reference-counted via skb_shared_info.

detail_nodes.title: Socket buffer limits
detail_nodes.description: Each socket has send and receive buffer limits initialized at creation. sk_sndbuf defaults to /proc/sys/net/core/wmem_default (typically ~16KB), and sk_rcvbuf defaults to rmem_default. These limits control how much data can be queued in the socket before the kernel starts dropping or blocking.

main_flow.title: Protocol Stack
main_flow.description: When data is sent through a socket, it traverses the protocol stack: the socket layer calls tcp_sendmsg(), which builds sk_buffs, then tcp_transmit_skb() adds TCP headers and passes to ip_queue_xmit(), which adds IP headers and routes to the network device. The receive path is the reverse: NIC → IP → TCP → socket receive queue.

detail_nodes.title: tcp_transmit_skb()
detail_nodes.description: tcp_transmit_skb() is the core TCP transmission function. It clones or allocates an sk_buff, builds the TCP header (source/dest ports, sequence numbers, flags), computes the checksum, and passes the packet to the IP layer via ip_queue_xmit() or ip_build_and_send_pkt().

detail_nodes.title: ip_queue_xmit() — IP layer
detail_nodes.description: ip_queue_xmit() is the IP layer transmission entry point for TCP. It looks up the routing table (via sk->sk_dst_cache), builds the IP header (version, length, TTL, protocol=TCP, source/dest addresses), computes the IP checksum, and passes the packet to the output device via dev_queue_xmit().

detail_nodes.title: dev_queue_xmit() — network device
detail_nodes.description: dev_queue_xmit() is the final kernel step before the packet reaches the NIC. It enqueues the sk_buff on the device's transmit queue (qdisc), triggers the device's hard_start_xmit method, and handles queue-full conditions by dropping or congesting.

detail_nodes.title: Receive path overview
detail_nodes.description: The receive path is the mirror image: the NIC raises an interrupt, the driver calls netif_rx() or napi_gro_receive(), the packet traverses the IP layer (ip_rcv()), the TCP layer (tcp_v4_rcv()), and finally is enqueued on the socket's receive queue (sk->sk_receive_queue) where it waits for the application to call recv().

main_flow.title: Return Path
main_flow.description: After the socket object is fully initialized, sock_map_fd() returns the new file descriptor. sys_socket() returns this fd through the syscall return path back to user space. The application can now use this fd with bind(), connect(), send(), recv(), and other socket operations.

detail_nodes.title: File descriptor return value
detail_nodes.description: The return value from socket() is a non-negative integer file descriptor (typically 3 or higher, since 0-2 are stdin/stdout/stderr). This fd indexes into the process's file descriptor table, where the entry points to a struct file whose private_data is the struct socket.

detail_nodes.title: Syscall return — sysret
detail_nodes.description: sys_socket() returns the fd to the syscall dispatch in entry_64.S. The RESTORE_ARGS macro reloads the saved user-space registers, and the sysretq instruction atomically restores %rip, %rflags, and switches back to ring 3. The C library wrapper receives the fd in %rax.

source_ref.snippet:
sysret_check:
  LOCKDEP_SYS_EXIT
  DISABLE_INTERRUPTS(CLBR_NONE)
  movl %_TIF_ALLWORK_MASK,%edi
  andl %edi,%edx
  jnz sysret_careful
  RESTORE_ARGS 0,-ARG_SKIP,0
  movq PER_CPU_VAR(old_rsp), %rsp
  USERGS_SYSRET64

detail_nodes.title: User space usage pattern
detail_nodes.description: The typical usage pattern is: fd = socket(AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM, 0); bind(fd, &local_addr, ...); connect(fd, &remote_addr, ...); send(fd, buf, len, 0); recv(fd, buf, len, 0); close(fd). Each call routes through the socket's proto_ops and then the transport protocol's proto vectors.
